fact.title: Let slugs run to 80 characters
fact.body:
Long post titles lose their meaning when the slug is cut at 40 characters.

`slugify` in `src/slug.ts` should cut at 80 characters, not 40. A cut slug must still not end on a `-`.

The law in `src/slug.laws.test.ts` holds slugs to 40 today, so it has to say 80 as well.

Yes: next is plan.

No other tickets exist and no rule for a no applies; the ticket asks for a clear, specified change to the cut length in `slugify` and its law, which a builder can plan and make. I did not inspect the repo, as the working directory is empty.

# Plan: Let slugs run to 80 characters

Allow post slugs up to 80 characters while keeping trailing hyphens out. Update the law in a separate PR first.

Size: 1 story, 2 tasks, 4 criteria, 315 words.

## User stories

- **S1**: As Blog author, I want Long post titles to retain up to 80 characters in their slugs, so that Cutting at 40 characters removes meaningful words..

## Rule changes

These land first, in a pull request of their own, on your yes. With the one for the tasks, this plan makes two pull requests.

- `src/slug.laws.test.ts`: In T1's separate PR, change 40 to 80 in the law comment and length assertion. Preserve the trailing-hyphen assertion. Why: The current law rejects the longer slugs explicitly requested by the ticket.

## Task 1: T1: Update the length law in a separate PR

It ends in a pull request.

- [ ] `c1 v1` When A reviewer reads the slug length law, The documented and asserted maximum is 80 characters.
  - **The whole job.** _Serves S1. Check (read): Read the law comment and its length assertion._  
    _Fixture: The existing law with generated titles up to 300 characters and seed 1._

## Task 2: T2: Extend slugs to 80 characters

It ends in a pull request.

- [ ] `c2 v1` When A blog author generates a slug for a long post title, The slug retains the first 80 normalized characters, with a trailing hyphen removed.
  - **The whole job.** _Serves S1. Check (test): Generate the fixture slug once and compare its full output._  
    _Fixture: One title: 'A practical guide to growing tomatoes on small balconies through the summer months'. Expected slug: 'a-practical-guide-to-growing-tomatoes-on-small-balconies-through-the-summer-mont'._

## The whole plan

Judged once every task is in, at the head of the pull request that holds them.

- [ ] `c3 v1` When A blog author generates a slug after both changes land, A long title retains meaningful text through the 80-character limit, with no trailing hyphen.
  - **The whole job.** _Serves S1. Check (test): In the final PR, verify the long-title output and the 80-character cutoff cases against the updated laws._  
    _Fixture: Generate each once: the 82-character title 'A practical guide to growing tomatoes on small balconies through the summer months', expecting 'a-practical-guide-to-growing-tomatoes-on-small-balconies-through-the-summer-mont'; and a title whose normalized slug has 79 letters followed by a hyphen and another word, expecting those 79 letters._
- [ ] `c4 v1` When The combined change receives its final review, The documented slug limit agrees with the 80-character behavior.
  - _Serves S1. Check (read): Read the updated law comment alongside the long-title acceptance examples._

## Open questions

None.

## Pointers (they bind nobody)

- `src/slug.laws.test.ts`: T1 owns the law comment and maximum assertion change; its PR precedes T2.
- `src/slug.ts`: T2 owns the maximum change from 40 to 80 in the existing slugify helper.
- `src/slug.test.ts`: T2 owns regression coverage for longer slugs and the new cutoff boundary.
- `AGENTS.md`: Requires adjacent helper tests, identifies law files, and prohibits runtime dependencies.

What each answer does:
- `approve`: The plan stands as written. The lane goes on with it.
- `no`: The lane ends here, and this change does not land.

fact.body:
These mutants lived, and the test writer says no test can see the change:
- `src/slug.ts:9:12:329f80`: Both regexes globally delete every Unicode mark using an empty replacement. The original deletes runs of marks; the mutant deletes each mark individually. They produce identical strings immediately after this replacement. Separator normalization, trimming, the 80-character cut, and final hyphen removal therefore receive identical input and return identical slugs. No test can distinguish them.

What each answer does:
- `again`: The test writer step runs once more, from the start.
- `go_on`: The lane moves on to the review step as things stand.
- `stop`: The lane ends here, and this change does not land.
